record.context_brief: Characterization problem for congruence lattices of patch lattices
record.original_question: Let D be a finite distributive lattice that is the glued sum D^h u B2 of a finite distributive lattice D^h with B2, and let L be a patch lattice, meaning a rectangular lattice whose corners are dual atoms; equivalently, patch lattices are exactly those rectangular lattices L for which Con L is a glued sum of a finite distributive lattice Con^h L with B2. Which properties of the finite distributive lattice Con^h L characterize exactly when D is the congruence lattice of a patch lattice L?

evidence.quote: Let D be a finite distributive lattice of the form DhuB2, the glued sum of a finite distributive lattice Dh with B2. One can think of Dh as D with the hat removed.

Recall that a rectangular lattice L is a patch lattice, if the corners are dual atoms. It is easy to verify that a rectangular lattice L is a patch lattice iff ConL is a glued sum of a finite distributive lattice Conh L with B2.
Patch Problem. Characterize the congruence lattice of a patch lattice L in terms of the properties of the finite distributive lattice Conh L.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions:

- A finite lattice L is called rectangular if it is planar, semimodular, and has exactly two doubly irreducible elements on its boundary, called its left corner and right corner; these corners are complementary elements. A rectangular lattice L is a patch lattice if its left and right corners are both dual atoms of L (i.e., are covered by the top element 1_L).

- For lattices, the glued sum A ⊔ B of two bounded lattices A and B is the lattice obtained by identifying the top element of A with the bottom element of B. Let B_2 denote the four-element Boolean lattice.

- The congruence lattice Con L of a finite lattice L is a finite distributive lattice. It is known that a rectangular lattice L is a patch lattice if and only if Con L can be written as a glued sum Con L = Con^h L ⊔ B_2 for some finite distributive lattice Con^h L (intuitively, Con^h L is Con L with its "hat" B_2 removed).

Problem: Determine necessary and sufficient conditions, expressed purely in terms of intrinsic properties of a finite distributive lattice D^h, for the finite distributive lattice D = D^h ⊔ B_2 to be isomorphic to Con L for some patch lattice L. Equivalently, characterize the class of finite distributive lattices that arise as Con^h L when L ranges over all patch lattices.
artifact.status_search_result: The Patch Problem is posed as an open characterization problem in Grätzer's work on congruences of finite lattices. Searches turned up Grätzer's monograph "The Congruences of a Finite Lattice: A Proof-by-Picture Approach" (latest edition 2023) and related notes, but no published solution characterizing congruence lattices of patch lattices in terms of Con^h L. Status is consistent with the problem remaining open.

status_evidence.title: The Congruences of a Finite Lattice: A Proof-by-Picture Approach (3rd ed., 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Grätzer's monograph surveying open problems on congruences of finite lattices, including rectangular and patch lattices.
status_evidence.claim: The Patch Problem is treated as an open characterization problem in current references on congruences of finite lattices.

status_evidence.title: Two Problems That Shaped a Century of Lattice Theory (Grätzer)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of central open problems on congruence lattices of finite lattices.
status_evidence.claim: Characterization problems for congruence lattices in restricted classes of finite lattices remain a central open theme.
